html:
SMTO-GML-0007 — The email's attachments are too big to send

GUID: 9ed9aa7c-40ef-4be5-9320-aab56db9e904
Slug: gmail-attachments-too-large
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • All the files together are bigger than the 25 MB that one email can carry. SMTO stopped before sending or saving the email, so nothing went out.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to send the email again with only the files the person really needs. Removing some files brings the total under the 25 MB limit.
  2. If every file is needed, ask SMTO to split them across two or more emails, each under 25 MB. The limit applies to each email, so several smaller emails can carry all the files.
  3. If you were forwarding an email, ask SMTO to forward it without its original attachments, or not as an attached copy of the email. The original email and its files count toward the same 25 MB limit.
  4. For a very large file, put it in shared online storage and ask SMTO to send a link instead. A link has no size limit in the email.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports the email as sent or drafted, and it appears in Gmail with the files you chose.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't send partly cut files; send whole files across several emails instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The combined size of the outgoing Gmail attachments (including a forwarded original message or forwarded attachments) exceeds the 25 MiB limit, so MIME construction stopped before any draft or send.

What this means

  • Aggregate outgoing attachment bytes exceed MAX_BYTES, or forwarded attachments exceed the forwarding allowance. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Aggregate outgoing attachment bytes exceed MAX_BYTES, or forwarded attachments exceed the forwarding allowance.

How to diagnose it

  • Measure complete attachment byte totals for the actual operation and preserve their exact contents.

How to fix it

  • The total attachment bytes exceeded MAX_BYTES (25 MiB) in gmail/files.py or the forward path in GmailService._mime. Remove or replace attachments, split them across several messages, or forward without include_attachments/as_attachment; never truncate attachment bytes.
  • Reduce or batch attachments to the supported size; do not truncate attachment bytes.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate supported message split or attachment selection stays within bounds.

What not to do

  • Do not erase authoritative receipts or protected current input to conceal a size/capacity problem.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
